COSM.01.note: Stanford's philosophy-of-time entry maps the main disputes about passage, persistence, past and future reality, and time's relation to physics.

exercise.prompt: Compare presentism, eternalism, and the growing-block view in a table, including what each says exists now.

COSM.02.note: The Stanford entry separates thermodynamic irreversibility, statistical mechanics, boundary conditions, and the arrow of time instead of reducing entropy to vague disorder.

exercise.prompt: Describe one reversible microscopic process and one irreversible macroscopic process, then identify the statistical assumption connecting them.

COSM.03.note: The SETI Institute presents the paradox, its assumptions, the Drake-equation context, and major families of proposed resolutions.

exercise.prompt: List five possible filters or explanations for the silence, then rank them by how much evidence would be needed to distinguish them.

COSM.04.note: Einstein Online's Elementary Einstein collection provides connected introductions to special relativity, spacetime, gravity, and general relativity.

article.title: Elementary Einstein
article.source: Einstein Online — Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

exercise.prompt: Calculate the Lorentz factor at several fractions of light speed and explain why Newtonian time is a good approximation at everyday speeds.

COSM.05.note: The Nobel Prize's 2022 popular information explains entanglement, Bell inequalities, and the experiments that ruled out broad classes of local hidden-variable models.

article.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2022 — Popular Information

exercise.prompt: Write a plain-language explanation of correlation, entanglement, and Bell inequality violation without using faster-than-light messaging as an explanation.

COSM.06.note: OpenStax develops double-slit interference quantitatively and shows how path difference produces bright and dark fringes.

exercise.prompt: Use the double-slit fringe-spacing formula to predict how the pattern changes when wavelength, slit spacing, or screen distance is doubled.

COSM.07.note: NASA's universe overview distinguishes ordinary matter, dark matter, and dark energy and summarizes the observations used to infer each component.

exercise.prompt: Create an evidence table for dark matter and dark energy, separating what is directly observed from what is inferred.

COSM.08.note: CERN's official overview explains the Standard Model's matter particles, force carriers, Higgs field, successes, and known omissions.

exercise.prompt: Recreate the Standard Model table from memory, grouping quarks, leptons, and bosons and adding charge and force interaction notes.

COSM.09.note: David Wallace's review explains precisely why combining black-hole evaporation with ordinary quantum mechanics appears to destroy information.

article.title: Why Black Hole Information Loss is Paradoxical

exercise.prompt: Write the paradox as a sequence of assumptions and identify which assumption each major proposed resolution must reject or modify.

COSM.10.note: NASA's WMAP overview explains the microwave background as relic radiation and connects its measured fluctuations to the age, geometry, and composition of the universe.

exercise.prompt: Explain why the cosmic microwave background is not light from the Big Bang instant itself and what the anisotropy map measures.

COSM.11.note: NASA's discussion of dark energy and cosmic expansion provides the observational basis for considering long-term expansion-dominated futures, including increasingly cold and dilute outcomes.

exercise.prompt: Compare heat death, Big Crunch, and Big Rip scenarios by stating the required expansion behavior and the final availability of usable energy.

COSM.12.note: The Santa Fe Institute introduces complex-systems science through nonlinearity, collective dynamics, hierarchy, randomness, and emergence.

exercise.prompt: Choose an emergent system and identify its agents, local rules, feedback loops, macro-pattern, and why the macro-pattern is not written into any one rule.
